title: WhatsApp chats as court evidence - what courts actually require
p1:
A WhatsApp screenshot can look convincing… but can it actually win a case in court?

Many people assume that showing a chat on their phone is enough. The reality is more complicated.
p2:
Courts do not only look at the message content. They also care about whether the chat is genuine, complete, and properly presented. A cropped screenshot without context may raise questions about editing, missing messages, or authenticity.

One thing many people don’t know: the original device, proper records, and legal proof of authenticity can matter more than just a screenshot.
p3:
WhatsApp conversations can become important evidence in disputes, but keeping the full conversation, preserving details like dates and sender information, and avoiding unnecessary alterations can make a big difference.

A message may be true, but proving that it is reliable is a separate step.
conclusion: Have you ever saved a WhatsApp chat thinking it could be used as proof later? Do you think screenshots alone should be accepted as court evidence?
